title: Trim promise and closure bookkeeping on calls
motivation: Each return of a version that creates promises called `Fir_mark_promises_escaped` on a tracking list that was often empty. `Fir_assume_function`, which guards each call of a known closure, was an out-of-line call.
solution: `Fir2CCompiler` emits an inline test `if (local_promises != R_NilValue)` before `Fir_mark_promises_escaped`, and `Fir_assume_function` and `Fir_is_compiled_closure` move to `runtime_inline.h` as `static ALWAYS_INLINE`. The runtime also keeps the count `Rsh_ElidedDepth` of the active outermost elided pushes, which the vendored R declares and restores at a caught error. `Fir_push_env` and `Fir_push_env_elided` increment it, and the pop of the outermost elided frame sets the singleton's parent to `R_EmptyEnv`, so the singleton, a GC root, does not keep that parent alive. The from-R entry saves and restores the count with the other from-R globals. So the push and the pop of an outermost elided frame each still run one `SET_ENCLOS`.

files.client/rsh/src/fir2c/runtime.c: Increments `Rsh_ElidedDepth` in the elided push, sets `R_EmptyEnv` in the pop of the outermost elided frame, saves and restores the depth at the from-R entry, and removes the out-of-line closure tests.
files.client/rsh/src/fir2c/runtime.h: Adds the depth parameter to the from-R set and unset functions, documents the pop of the outermost elided frame, and removes two out-of-line declarations.
files.client/rsh/src/fir2c/runtime_inline.h: The inline elided push and pop keep `Rsh_ElidedDepth`; adds `Fir_is_compiled_closure` and `Fir_assume_function` as `static ALWAYS_INLINE`.
files.server/src/main/java/org/prlprg/fir2c/Fi: The from-R entry saves and restores the elided depth, and a return calls `Fir_mark_promises_escaped` only on a non-empty tracking list.
files.server/src/test/resources/org/prlprg/exa: New example where `gc()` must collect the parent of the outermost elided frame after it returns.
New example where an error caught in a callee skips the pop of an elided frame, and `gc()` must still collect that frame's parent.
